headline: Real yields punched to a new high and the euro printed a 52-week low — yesterday's dollar reprieve is over, and this time Europe, not the S&P, is paying for it.
summary: The rates pause lasted one day. The 5y is +5bp to 5.06% (98th percentile, +52bp on the month, z=1.69), the 10y +4bp to 5.28% (99th percentile), the 30y 5.63%, and the 10-year real yield made another new high at 2.92% with z=1.84 and acceleration 1.33. Critically, none of it is inflation: 10y breakevens 2.36% (+2bp on the month, z=0.08) and 5y breakevens are rolling over with acceleration -0.32. This is term premium plus a hawkish front end — the 3m bill is +27bp on the month to 4.19% as cuts get priced out, and 3m10y at +1.09 sits at the 100th percentile of the year. The rates composite deteriorated from -76 to -78, the worst reading on the board, and MOVE is +11.8% on the week and +34.6% on the month at 107.29 (z=1.88) even after a 0.8% down day.

What changed today is the dollar. Yesterday the dollar looked like it had stopped; today EURUSD at 1.1257 is at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks (-2.9% on the month, z=-1.44, acceleration -1.2), DXY is turning up again with acceleration 1.06 at the 97th percentile, and Europe broke: Euro Stoxx -1.5%, CAC -1.6%, FTSE -1.7%, EWI -2.5%, EWP -2.3%, EWG -1.2%, and EFA/SPY at the 0th percentile of the year. EM is now pure dispersion rather than a bloc: Bovespa +2.6% on the day and +4.7% on the week at the 89th percentile, while USDMXN (z=2.60, acceleration 2.12, the most extreme print on the board) keeps EWW -7.8% on the month, Sensex sits at the 0th percentile with INDA -6.5%, TUR -13.6%, ARGT -11.6%, EZA -9.6%. The one clean exception is North Asia: USDKRW -1.1% to 1342 (-12.9% on three months) with EWY +5.9% on the month, the Nikkei +5.3% on the week and TWII at the 100th percentile.

US internals stopped getting worse, which is the modest good news. RSP/SPY +0.3% and IWM/SPY +0.2% lifted the breadth z from -2.11 to -1.91, MDY +1.0% turned up, DJT +2.1%, RUT +0.9% and KRE turned up — the first day in a week the average stock didn't lose ground to the index. Leadership is unchanged though: SOXX +15.3% and SMH +13.3% on the month, AMD +34.0% (z=1.67, 64.9% above its 200d), MU +17.6%, META +25.6% (z=2.03), QQQ/SPY z=1.70, high-beta/low-vol at the 100th percentile. And equity vol is still priced as if the bond market doesn't exist: VIX -6.6% to 15.31 (10th percentile), VIX3M 18.01 (5th percentile), term structure 0.85 — against a MOVE at the 87th percentile. That gap is the cheapest asymmetry available.

Beneath the index the tape is splitting cleanly along the discount rate. Energy and growth cyclicals work — Brent 102.70 (+7.4% on the month), XOP +2.8%, XLE +2.0%, copper +1.5% with copper/gold +2.2% to the 96th percentile (acceleration 1.47), growth composite +20. The rate-sensitive consumer is being dismantled with no defensive shelter: 30y mortgage 7.28% at the 100th percentile (+62bp on the month, z=1.85, acceleration 1.27), HD -11.0% at the 0th percentile, MCD z=-2.39, NKE and NFLX at the 0th percentile, XHB/SPY at the 2.5th. Financials remain in open liquidation despite the steepest 3m10y of the year — BX -17.9% on the month (z=-1.85), GS -10.6%, IAI -7.6%, XLF -6.2%. Credit is the one hinge still holding: HYG/IEF +0.4% at the 89th percentile and BKLN at the 90th say spreads are fine, but HYG itself is -2.3% on the month with z=-1.5 and acceleration -1.07. HY's pain is duration, not default — until it isn't, and that is the line to watch.

good.text: Credit still refuses to crack. HYG/IEF +0.4% on the month at the 89th percentile, BKLN at the 90th, and the credit & vol composite holds at 42 — spreads are absorbing a 49bp monthly rise in the 10y without widening.

Participation stopped bleeding. RSP/SPY +0.3% and IWM/SPY +0.2% lifted the breadth z from -2.11 to -1.91, with MDY +1.0% turning up, DJT +2.1%, RUT +0.9% and KRE turning up — the first non-deteriorating internals day in a week.
The cyclical signal is real, not inflationary. Copper +1.5%, copper/gold +2.2% to the 96th percentile with acceleration 1.47, DBC +1.3%, growth composite +20 — while 10y breakevens sit flat at 2.36%.

AI leadership is widening within tech rather than narrowing to one name: SOXX +15.3% and SMH +13.3% on the month, MU +17.6%, AMD +34.0%, TSM +11.2%, CIBR +7.9% at the 99th percentile, XLK relative strength +7.3%.

North Asia is the one offshore market compounding: Nikkei +5.3% on the week, EWY +5.9% on the month, TWII at the 100th percentile — and USDKRW -1.1% to 1342 means it is happening with a firming local currency, not a devaluation.

bad.text: The entire curve backed up again: 2y +5bp to 4.83%, 5y +5bp to 5.06% (z=1.69), 10y 5.28% at the 99th percentile, 10y real yield 2.92% with acceleration 1.33. Rates composite worsened from -76 to -78 — the single worst input on the board, and it is accelerating in the wrong direction.

Bond vol versus equity vol is a dislocation, not a view. MOVE +11.8% on the week and +34.6% on the month (z=1.88, 87th percentile) against VIX 15.31 at the 10th percentile and VIX3M at the 5th. Equity hedges are mispriced against the asset actually moving.

The dollar re-accelerated and Europe is the casualty: EURUSD 1.1257 at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks, DXY turning up with acceleration 1.06, USDCAD at the 100th percentile, USDMXN z=2.60 with acceleration 2.12. EFA/SPY is at the 0th percentile with EWI -2.5% and EWP -2.3% on the day.

Rate transmission to the consumer is now brutal: 30y mortgage 7.28% at the 100th percentile (+62bp on the month, acceleration 1.27), HD -11.0% at the 0th percentile, MCD z=-2.39, NKE and NFLX at the 0th, ITB -14.4% on three months, XHB/SPY at the 2.5th percentile.

Financials keep liquidating into the steepest 3m10y of the year — BX -17.9% on the month (z=-1.85), GS -10.6% (z=-1.61), IAI -7.6%, KIE z=-1.60, JPM -6.1%, XLF relative strength -6.7%. When the curve steepens and banks still fall, it is funding and marks, not margin.

Thematic liquidation is accelerating downward, not basing: REMX -17.4% on the month (acceleration -1.87, 1st percentile), NLR -11.2% (acceleration -1.70, 0.1 percentile), URA -9.9%, TAN at the 0.2 percentile, XME -9.9% with acceleration -1.74, GDX acceleration -2.50 and GDX/GOLD -2.69.

trades.name: Buy index downside while vol is at the 10th percentile
trades.line: Long SPX put spread — VIX 15.3 (10th pct) vs MOVE at 107
trades.expr: Buy a Dec SPX ~5%/11% OTM put spread (7350/6900 strikes against 7722 spot), 50-75bp of premium; or long VIX Nov 20/30 call spread as the convex version.
trades.thesis: Equity vol is priced for a world where the 10y isn't at 5.28% and the 10y real yield isn't making new highs with acceleration 1.33. Bond vol has already repriced; equity vol hasn't. You are buying the cheapest leg of a two-leg macro shock.
trades.trigger: VIX -6.6% to 15.31 (10th percentile), VIX3M 18.01 (5th percentile), term structure 0.85 — on the same day MOVE sits +34.6% on the month at z=1.88 and the 5y/10y both added another 4-5bp.
trades.stop: MOVE back under 95 with the 10y below 5.05% — the rates shock dissipates and the hedge is dead money; cut at 50% premium loss.
trades.target: VIX 24-26, SPX 6-8% lower; 3-4x on the put spread.

trades.name: Short EUR/USD
trades.line: Short EURUSD at 1.1257 — 52-week low, dollar re-accelerating
trades.expr: Short EURUSD spot or Dec EUR future; ETF version long UUP against short FXE. Add on any retrace to 1.1350.
trades.thesis: The dollar pause ended. With US 5y at 5.06% and the front end pricing out cuts (3m bill +27bp on the month), carry and growth differentials both favour the dollar, and European equity is already confirming — EFA/SPY at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks.
trades.trigger: EURUSD 1.1257 is the 0th percentile of the year, -2.9% on the month with z=-1.44 and acceleration -1.2; DXY turning up at the 97th percentile with acceleration 1.06; Euro Stoxx -1.5%, CAC -1.6%, EWI -2.5%, EWP -2.3% on the day.
trades.stop: 1.1480 — back inside the prior month's range, or DXY back below 100.5.

trades.name: Long HYG vs short LQD
trades.line: Long HYG / short LQD — own the spread, not the duration
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long HYG, short LQD. Institutional version: long CDX HY risk vs short IG duration via 10y futures.
trades.thesis: The bond selloff is a real-rate event, not a credit event. LQD's damage is pure duration; HY's spread component is still the strongest part of the risk complex. This isolates the part that's working and shorts the part that only loses when the 10y rises.
trades.trigger: LQD -2.6% on the month at the 4th percentile of 52 weeks while HYG/IEF is +0.4% at the 89th percentile and BKLN at the 90th; the 10y added 49bp on the month with breakevens flat at 2.36%.
trades.stop: HYG/IEF breaks its 200d (currently 2.6% above) — that flips the driver from duration to spread and the pair stops working.

trades.name: Long GEV + ETN vs short CEG + VST + NLR
trades.line: Long GEV/ETN vs short CEG/VST/NLR — equipment over electrons
trades.expr: Equal-weight long GEV and ETN against an equal-weight short basket of CEG, VST and NLR, dollar-neutral.
trades.thesis: The power trade has bifurcated: order books for grid and electrical equipment keep compounding while the IPP/nuclear equity story is being de-rated by a 5.28% 10y and falling power-price optimism. Own the cash-flow-now side, short the discounted-terminal-value side.
trades.trigger: GEV +3.9% on the day, +9.9% on the month with acceleration 1.03; ETN +11.9% on the month, z=1.23 with acceleration 1.53; GRID turning up. Against CEG -7.6% on the month at the 14th percentile, VST at the 7th, NLR -11.2% at the 0.1 percentile with acceleration -1.70.
trades.stop: NLR reclaims its 200d (20.5% away) or ETN's acceleration flips negative with GEV losing 10% from here.

trades.name: Long EWZ vs short EWW
trades.line: Long EWZ / short EWW — Brazil bid, the peso is the problem
trades.expr: 1:1 notional long EWZ, short EWW. Overlay: short MXN forwards if you want the FX leg standalone.
trades.thesis: EM is no longer a bloc. Brazil has commodity tailwinds (Brent +7.4% on the month, copper at the 89th percentile) and a currency that has held; Mexico has the single most extreme FX move on the board and an equity market in free relative decline.
trades.trigger: Bovespa +2.6% on the day, +4.7% on the week, +10.2% on three months at the 89th percentile. EWW -7.8% on the month with relative strength -8.3%, -1.9% on the day, and USDMXN z=2.60 with acceleration 2.12.
trades.stop: USDBRL through 5.40 (it turned up today, +0.8%) or USDMXN back under 17.60.

trades.name: Short home construction (ITB)
trades.line: Short ITB — 7.28% mortgage is a 100th-percentile extreme
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy Jan ITB puts ~8% OTM; beta-neutral version is short ITB against long SPY at 1:1 notional.
trades.thesis: The mortgage rate is the cleanest transmission of the real-yield shock, and it is still accelerating. Builder margins and order books have not yet reflected 7.28% financing; the stocks have only partially.
trades.trigger: 30y mortgage 7.28%, 100th percentile of 52 weeks, +62bp on the month with z=1.85 and acceleration 1.27; ITB -14.4% on three months at the 7.5th percentile, XHB/SPY at the 2.5th, DHI -13.3% on three months, HD -11.0% at the 0th percentile.
trades.stop: 10y back under 5.00% or mortgage under 7.00%; or ITB reclaims its 200d, 9.5% above here.

trades.name: Long IBIT (small, with MSTR as the levered leg)
trades.line: Long IBIT — whole crypto complex flipped to turning up
trades.expr: Long IBIT at 1-1.5% of book; express the beta via MSTR Jan call spreads rather than more spot.
trades.thesis: Risk appetite is reviving in the most liquidity-sensitive corner of the market from a deeply damaged base — BTC is still -30.8% year-over-year at only the 39th percentile of 52 weeks, so this is recovery, not froth. The whole complex flipped trend state together, which rarely happens by accident.
trades.trigger: BTC +4.1% on the month and +34.1% on three months, ETH +6.8%/+50.6%, SOL +14.7% on the month, IBIT +9.6%, MSTR +4.8% on the day and +28.5% on the month — all states turning up, with relative strength versus the S&P turning up alongside.
trades.stop: BTC back below 78,000 or IBIT failing at its 200d (14.5% above spot).
